## Outcome

I started PR #343, exploring how histogram bins can update after an interactive selection.

## What I Did

- Began from [Issue #158](https://github.com/animint/animint2/issues/158).
- Added a failing acceptance test first.
- Required both changing counts after selection and fixed bin boundaries for meaningful comparison.
- Exported raw values and a stable set of breaks from R.
- Added a JavaScript `stat-bin.js` path to recompute counts in the browser.
- Refreshed affected histogram geometry after selection.
- Continued review updates on PR #336 and PR #261.
- Synchronized PR #339 and collaborative PR #253 with current `master`.

## Learnings

Interactive statistical transforms are not equivalent to filtering precomputed rows. When selected data changes, the statistic may need to be recomputed. For histograms, fixed breaks are essential; otherwise a changing bin grid prevents meaningful visual comparison.

## Challenges / Notes

This was a proof of concept, not a finished general framework for browser-side statistical transforms. Its open status and limitations remain visible.

## Next Week Targets

Finish the acceptance path, stabilize coverage, merge multiline text, and prepare the final report.
